NAMO DRONE DIDI — OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR WOMEN SHG AGRICULTURAL DRONES

Section 1: Financial Assistance and Capital Grant Structure
- Under the Namo Drone Didi scheme, Women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) receive Central Financial Assistance (subsidy) at 80% of the drone and accessory cost, up to a maximum of Rs. 8,00,000 per drone package.
- The remaining 20% of the drone procurement cost may be raised as a credit facility under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) with an interest subvention of 3% per annum.
- Under related SMAM norms, individual small and marginal farmers are eligible for a maximum subsidy of 50% up to Rs. 5,00,000 per drone, whereas Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) receive up to 75% grant for community demonstration drones.

Section 2: Drone Pilot Training, Eligibility, and Monthly Stipend
- One qualified woman member aged between 18 years and 45 years from each selected Women SHG shall undergo mandatory Remote Pilot Training of 15 days duration at an approved RPTO.
- A second woman member from the same SHG shall receive 5 days of specialized drone assistant and maintenance training.
- Each certified Women SHG drone pilot (Drone Didi) receives a monthly living stipend of Rs. 15,000 per month based on verified spraying operations.
- Each Drone Didi cluster is expected to cover at least 2,000 acres of agricultural land annually across fertilizers and nano-urea spraying operations.
- Private corporate entities, large commercial estates, and income tax payers are excluded and not eligible for the 80% Women SHG drone grant.
